title: Interior mutability: Cell and RefCell
summary: Mutation through a shared reference - with the borrow rules enforced at runtime instead.
lecture: Sometimes an API must mutate through &self - caches, counters, observers. Interior mutability moves the one-writer-XOR-many-readers check from compile time to somewhere else: Cell<T> for Copy values (get/set whole values, no references handed out, no way to fail), RefCell<T> for everything else (borrow()/borrow_mut() return guards, violations PANIC at runtime).

The RefCell footgun is guard lifetime: a named guard (`let snapshot = cell.borrow();`) stays live until it drops - a borrow_mut() while it lives panics, even though everything compiled. A temporary (`cell.borrow().len()`) drops at the end of its statement, which is usually what you wanted.

Runtime checks are a real cost and a real risk - 'already borrowed' panics ship to production. Reach for Cell first (it can't panic), RefCell only when you must lend references, and treat every named guard as a live wire: scope it tight.

example.caption: Cell can't fail; RefCell trades compile errors for runtime panics - scope the guards.
